findings.title: Authorization fragment returned without parentheses; AND-composition leaks rows
findings.body: The org and team builders join their branches with a bare `OR` (line 173 for org, line 206 for team), and the reduce returns that join unwrapped. `getAuthorizationConditions()` (line 83-88) and `getBaseConditions()` with no filters (line 74-75) therefore return a top-level `(A) OR (B)` fragment. The old code returned `{ AND: [{ OR: [...] }] }`, which Prisma nests safely. Raw SQL does not: a caller who writes `WHERE ${base} AND "timeStatus" = 'completed'` gets `(A) OR ((B) AND ...)`, so org-wide team bookings are returned without the caller's predicate. The same issue applies to `getFilterConditions()` when only `eventTypeId` is set: lines 105-107 return `("eventTypeId" = X) OR ("eventParentId" = X)` unwrapped. `getBaseConditions()` hides that case only because it wraps both sides when filters exist. Fix: wrap each returned fragment in parentheses (for example `Prisma.sql\`(${joined})\``) at the return of the reduce in buildOrgAuthorizationCondition, buildTeamAuthorizationCondition and buildFilterConditions. The integration tests at lines 296-299, 332-343 and 384-386 pin the unwrapped form, so they would need updating too. No caller in the repository uses these methods at head (the only references are this file and its test), so nothing breaks today; this is a defect in an exported, composable API.
findings.originReason: The diff replaced the Prisma where-object composition (which nests safely) with raw Prisma.sql fragments joined by a bare OR; the old code returned { AND: [{ OR: [...] }] }.

verification.reason: The org/team reducers return `(A) OR (B)` and the eventTypeId filter returns `(X) OR (Y)` with no outer parentheses, and getAuthorizationConditions/getBaseConditions (line 75) pass these through unwrapped, so appending `AND pred` binds only to the last branch. No caller in the repo composes these at head (only the file and its test reference them), so this is a hazard in the API, not a live leak; dropping to consider.

findings.title: getBaseConditions test never composes the fragment with another predicate
findings.body: The only getBaseConditions test (lines 438-501) runs `WHERE ${baseConditions}` on its own and nothing else. The precedence problem in insightsBooking.ts:173 needs a caller that adds `AND` after the fragment, so this test cannot fail on it. Add a case that appends an extra predicate, for example an `AND "timeStatus" = 'uncompleted'` (or a status filter), with a scope that yields an OR, and assert that rows outside the authorization scope are not returned.
findings.originReason: The getBaseConditions test was added by this diff and only uses the fragment on its own.

verification.reason: The only getBaseConditions test runs `WHERE ${baseConditions}` on its own, with user scope (no OR in auth), so it cannot catch precedence problems when another predicate is added.

findings.title: Caching tests removed with no replacement
findings.body: The PR deletes the `describe("Caching")` block, which checked that getAuthorizationConditions() and getFilterConditions() return the cached value on a second call. Nothing in the head file now covers the `cachedAuthConditions` and `cachedFilterConditions` memoization (insightsBooking.ts:83-95), including the cached `null` for filters. If the removal is intentional, say so in the PR; otherwise restore a memoization test in the new `Prisma.Sql` form.
findings.originReason: The diff deletes the describe("Caching") block and adds nothing in its place.

verification.reason: A case-insensitive search for cache/Caching in the head test file finds nothing, so the memoization in getAuthorizationConditions/getFilterConditions (lines 83-95) is no longer tested.

findings.title: Null branches in getBaseConditions are unreachable
findings.body: `getAuthorizationConditions()` is typed `Promise<Prisma.Sql>` and always returns an object: NOTHING_CONDITION or a built fragment (lines 83-88, 125-143). The `authConditions` checks at lines 72-80 are therefore always truthy, so the `else if (filterConditions)` branch (line 76-77) and the final `else` returning NOTHING_CONDITION (line 78-79) can never run. Either make the auth result nullable and handle it, or drop the dead branches so the logic reads as it actually behaves.

verification.reason: buildAuthorizationConditions always returns a Prisma.Sql object (NOTHING_CONDITION or a fragment, lines 125-143), and that object is always truthy, so the `else if (filterConditions)` and final `else` branches at lines 76-79 can never run.

findings.title: findMany removed; no in-repo callers at head
findings.body: The public `findMany` method (formerly lines 67-81) is gone, and the constructor now takes `InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions`. A grep of the head found no callers of InsightsBookingService outside this file and its integration test, so nothing in the repository breaks. Callers outside the repo, if any, would need to switch to `getBaseConditions()` plus raw `$queryRaw`.

contracts.action: getBaseConditions() returns a Prisma.Sql fragment that a caller splices into a raw WHERE clause
contracts.before_after: Before: findMany built a Prisma where object `{...where, AND: [auth, filter]}` and Prisma applied it. After: getBaseConditions returns a bare SQL fragment. Only the auth-plus-filter join is parenthesized; a fragment returned alone is not.
contracts.visible_effect: None today. No caller in the repository invokes getBaseConditions, so nothing reaches a screen.
contracts.failure_mode: A caller that appends AND after the fragment with no filters set and scope org or team gets `(A) OR (B) AND ...`, which returns rows outside the authorization scope. See the finding at insightsBooking.ts:173.

contracts.action: getAuthorizationConditions() memoizes the built fragment on the instance
contracts.before_after: Before and after both cache on the instance and rebuild only when the cache is undefined. Caching is unchanged apart from the type.
contracts.failure_mode: If buildAuthorizationConditions throws (for example a DB error in isOrgOwnerOrAdmin or teamRepo), the error propagates and nothing is cached, so a retry rebuilds. A stale result is possible only if options or DB membership change during one instance's lifetime, as before.

contracts.action: getFilterConditions() memoizes null or a fragment for eventTypeId and memberUserId filters
contracts.before_after: Before: the filter was a Prisma object or null, combined with AND by findMany. After: the filter is a bare fragment or null. With two filters, they are joined with parentheses (line 121). With only eventTypeId, the bare OR is returned unwrapped (line 106).
contracts.failure_mode: A direct caller of getFilterConditions() that uses the result with AND, with only eventTypeId set, gets an unparenthesized OR. See the finding at insightsBooking.ts:173.

summary: Reviewed insightsBooking.ts and its integration test. The raw-SQL rewrite keeps the column names (they match the BookingTimeStatusDenormalized view), parameterizes all values, and keeps the same authorization logic. The main defect is that the returned authorization and filter fragments are not parenthesized: the org and team builders return a bare `A OR B`, so any caller that appends AND gets rows outside its scope. That is a "fix" with medium confidence, because no caller in the repository uses these methods at head. The tests pin the unwrapped shape and never compose the fragment with another predicate, so they cannot catch it. The PR also drops the caching tests and leaves some unreachable null branches in getBaseConditions. No ADR directory exists at head, so there are no ADR findings.
